questions.question: The Preamble of the Constitution describes India as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a secular state**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble of the Constitution **of India describes the country as a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic**.
 
• The term **secular** indicates that the state has **no official religion** and treats all religions equally.
 
• This reflects the commitment of the Indian Constitution to maintain religious neutrality and ensure freedom of religion for all citizens.
 
• The Preamble serves as an introduction to the Constitution and sets forth the guiding principles and philosophy of the document.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It establishes the framework for the political principles, structures, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Preamble reflects the aspirations and values of the people of India, including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• The inclusion of the word "secular" in the Preamble was made through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• The Preamble is considered a part of the Constitution and is used to interpret ambiguous areas of the law.

questions.question: Oil India Limited (OIL) is under the administrative structure of:

• The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is responsible for the exploration, production, refining, distribution, marketing, import, export, and conservation of petroleum, natural gas, and petroleum products.
 
• OIL is a **government-owned company** that plays a crucial role in the energy sector of India, focusing on the exploration, development, and production of crude oil and natural gas.
 
• The Ministry oversees various public sector undertakings (PSUs) related to petroleum and natural gas, ensuring the energy security of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas** was formed in **1947 **and has since played a significant role in the development of the petroleum industry in India.
 
• The Ministry's responsibilities include policy formulation, coordination, and regulation of the petroleum and natural gas industries in India.
 
• It works towards ensuring the availability of petroleum products at reasonable prices and promotes the conservation of petroleum products.
 
• The Ministry is also involved in international cooperation and partnership in the energy sector to enhance India's energy security.
 
• OIL, under the Ministry's guidance, has expanded its operations both domestically and internationally, contributing significantly to India's energy needs.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations said that India CANNOT have a parallel judicial system - one for the rich and the other for the poor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India emphasized that the country cannot have a parallel judicial system - one for the rich and the other for the poor.
 
• This statement underscores the importance of equality before the law and the need for a uniform judicial system that serves all citizens equally, regardless of their socio-economic status.
 
• The Supreme Court is the **highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India**, and it has the power of judicial review.
 
• The Court's decision reflects its role in upholding the Constitution and ensuring justice is accessible to everyone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court of India** was established on **28th January 1950**, two days after the Constitution of India came into effect.
 
• It comprises the **Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 33 other judges**, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Supreme Court's primary function is to interpret the Constitution and adjudicate disputes between the central government and state governments or between two or more states.
 
• The Court also has the authority to hear appeals against the judgments of lower courts and tribunals.
 
• Through its judgments, the Supreme Court plays a crucial role in the development of constitutional law and the protection of fundamental rights in India.

questions.question: Who is known as the Father of Modern Dance in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uday Shankar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uday Shankar** is known as the **Father of Modern Dance** in India.
 
• He was a pioneer in adapting Western theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance forms, creating a new genre of modern Indian dance.
 
• Uday Shankar's innovative approach combined elements of Indian classical dance, folk traditions, and Western ballet, making dance accessible to a broader audience.
 
• His contributions significantly influenced the development of contemporary dance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uday Shankar** was born on 8th December 1900, in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India.
 
• He studied at the Royal College of Art in London, where he was introduced to Western art forms.
 
• In 1930, he established the Uday Shankar India Cultural Centre in Almora, which became a hub for training and innovation in Indian dance and music.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award, in **1971 **for his **contributions to the arts**.
 
• Uday Shankar's legacy continues to inspire dancers and choreographers in India and around the world.

questions.question: Who calculated the approximate location of the planet Neptune by studying gravity - induced disturbances in the motion of Uranus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urbain-Jean-Joseph Le Verrier**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urbain-Jean-Joseph Le Verrier** calculated the **approximate location of the planet Neptune **by studying gravity-induced disturbances in the motion of Uranus.
 
• Le Verrier's calculations were based on Newton's laws of gravitation, which predicted the presence of another planet affecting Uranus's orbit.
 
• His work led to the** discovery of Neptune on September 23, 1846, by Johann Gottfried Galle and Heinrich d'Arrest** at the **Berlin Observatory**.
 
• Le Verrier's prediction and the subsequent discovery of Neptune stand as a monumental achievement in the field of astronomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Couch Adams** independently made similar calculations around the same time, but Le Verrier's work led to the actual observational discovery.
 
• Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun and is known for its deep blue color caused by the absorption of red light by methane in its atmosphere.
 
• The discovery of Neptune was a major milestone in the validation of Newtonian mechanics.
 
• Le Verrier's methods of celestial mechanics continue to influence modern astronomy and space navigation.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is called ‘Singi Khamban’ in Tibet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The river **Indus** is known as '**Singi Khamban**' in Tibet.
 
• 'Singi Khamban' translates to the "**Lion's Mouth**" in Tibetan language, referring to the river's origin in the Tibetan plateau.
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the agricultural and economic activities of these regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus River originates in the **Tibetan plateau near Lake Mansarovar**.
 
• It flows through the Ladakh region of India and then into Pakistan, where it eventually** drains into the Arabian Sea**.
 
• The river is a key water source for the Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's oldest civilizations.
 
• The Indus Basin is shared by India and Pakistan, making it a significant geopolitical feature in South Asia.
 
• The river supports diverse ecosystems and is home to various species of fish and other aquatic life.

questions.question: Which Act opposed by Mahatma Gandhi in 1919 was a direct attack on the civil liberties and democratic rights of the Indian people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was enacted in **1919 **by the British government to curb the growing nationalist upsurge in India.
 
• This Act authorized the government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years.
 
• It also allowed the government to search any place and arrest any person without a warrant.
 
• The Act was seen as a direct attack on the civil liberties and democratic rights of the Indian people, leading to widespread protests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahatma Gandhi strongly opposed the Rowlatt Act and initiated a nationwide protest against it, which is known as the **Rowlatt Satyagraha**.
 
• The protests against the Rowlatt Act led to the tragic event of the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** in April 1919.
 
• The Act was officially known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**.
 
• The widespread opposition to the Rowlatt Act marked a significant moment in India's struggle for independence.

__
 
• **Simhavishnu** was the founder of the **Pallava dynasty**.
 
• The Pallava dynasty was a Tamil dynasty that ruled parts of South India from the 3rd century to the 9th century.
 
• Simhavishnu's reign marked the rise of the Pallavas to prominence in the region.
 
• The Pallavas are known for their patronage of architecture, particularly the rock-cut temples of Mahabalipuram.
 
• The dynasty played a crucial role in the cultural and political history of South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Their rule saw the construction of several notable temples, including the **Shore Temple and the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram**.
 
• Simhavishnu's successors, such as Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I, continued to expand the dynasty's influence and patronage of the arts.
 
• The Pallavas had a significant impact on the cultural and religious landscape of South India, with contributions to both Hinduism and Buddhism.

questions.question: The number of white pawns in chess is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **8 white pawns** in a standard game of chess.
 
• Each player starts with **8 pawns** positioned on the second row (rank) of their side of the board.
 
• The primary role of pawns is to advance forward and capture opponent pieces diagonally.
 
• While pawns are the least valuable pieces in terms of points, they play a crucial role in controlling the center of the board and supporting other pieces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In chess, each player starts with a total of **16 pieces**, including 8 pawns.
 
• The other pieces include **2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, 1 queen, and 1 king**.
 
• Pawns have the unique ability to promote to any other piece (except a king) if they reach the opponent's back rank (eighth rank for white, first rank for black).
 
• The movement and strategy involving pawns are fundamental aspects of chess openings and endgames.
 
• Pawns can execute a special move called "**en passant**" under specific conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the purchase and sale of government securities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Open market operations**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open market operations** refer to the **buying and selling of government securities **in the open market by a central bank.
 
• The primary aim of these operations is to regulate the money supply in the economy and control inflation.
 
• When the central bank buys securities, it injects liquidity into the banking system, which can help lower interest rates and stimulate economic activity.
 
• Conversely, selling securities withdraws liquidity from the market, which can help raise interest rates and curb inflation.
 
• Open market operations are a key tool used by central banks, such as the Federal Reserve in the United States and the Reserve Bank of India, to implement monetary policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High powered money** refers to the total currency in circulation and reserves held by banks with the central bank.
 
• **Reserve ratio** is the fraction of total deposits that a bank must hold in reserve and not lend out.
 
• **Bank rate** is the rate at which a central bank lends money to domestic banks, often used as a tool to control liquidity and inflation.
 
• The central bank uses these various tools to influence the economy, control inflation, and ensure financial stability.

questions.question: In honey bees, _____

options.text: males are diploid and females are haploid.
males are triploid and females are tetraploid.
males are haploid and females are diploid.
males are tetraploid and females are triploid.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**males are haploid and females are diploid**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In honey bees, males are haploid and females are diploid.**
 
• **Males (drones)** develop from unfertilized eggs and possess only **one set of chromosomes**.
 
• Females (workers and queens) develop from fertilized eggs and possess two sets of chromosomes.
 
• This is an example of a genetic system known as **haplodiploidy**.
 
• The haplodiploid system determines the sex of the offspring based on the number of chromosome sets they receive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haplodiploidy** is a common genetic system in several insect orders, including Hymenoptera (bees, ants, and wasps).
 
• In haplodiploid species, the sex determination mechanism can influence social structure and behavior, particularly in eusocial species like honey bees.
 
• **Queens can control the sex of their offspring by choosing whether to fertilize an egg**.
 
• This system allows for a high degree of relatedness among workers, which can promote cooperative behaviors.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true about the positive impact of the Green Revolution (GR) on yield levels in India?

i. During the post GR period, the yield of rice grew at a much faster rate than that of wheat.

ii. GR technology had penetrated more in wheat crop than in the rice crop.

iii. During post GR period, the area under rice achieved a relatively slow growth when compared to the area under wheat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only ii and iii**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **GR technology had penetrated more in wheat crop than in the rice crop.**
 
• During post GR period, the area under rice achieved a relatively slow growth when compared to the area under wheat.
 
• Option 4 is correct because statements ii and iii are true about the positive impact of the Green Revolution on yield leve
